messages.subject: Re: Memory problems with large-scale social network visualization using RCytoscape
parts:
Dear Ignacio,

I'd be glad to help -- and glad, too, that you are finding RCy useful.

Can you send me the script and the graph? That will be the easiest way for me to figure out the problem you encountered. Please run 'sessionInfo ()' within R, and include that too.

Cheers!

- Paul


On Apr 11, 2012, at 1:58 AM, I. Perez-Hallerbach wrote:

> Dear Dr Shannon,
>
> I hope this email finds you well. My apologies for writng to your private address as well - I just found it on the Cytoscape Google discussion group and thought I'd give it a try. First of all, I would like to thank you for developing RCytoscape, which I find immensely helpful in my current social network research at the University of Cambridge.
>
> Unfortunately, I have now run into a problem while using it and I was wondering whether you could help me solve it:
>
> I work on a Windows 7 Enterprise platform with the 32bit version of R and have about 3GB of RAM on my machine. I have large-scale social network data (c. 7,000 vertices and c. 30,000 edges) which are currently stored in my SQL database. I have managed to pull this data (omitting vertex and edge attributes) into an R dataframe and then into an igraph object. For further analysis and visualization, I would now like to push this igraph into Cytoscape using RCytoscape. Currently, my approach is to convert the igraph object into an graphNEL object since RCytoscape seems to work well with this object type.
>
> Unfortunately, I always run into memory issues when running this script. It has worked previously with smaller networks though.
>
> Could you please help me out?
>
> Any help would be much appreciated. Thanks so much in advance!
>
> Best, Ignacio
>
> Ignacio Pérez Hallerbach
> PhD student
> University of Cambridge
>
